    Airstream World Traveler 22RB

    £72,995

    By Peter Baber
    Published: September 1, 2026

    Listen to audio version of this article
    Sponsored by
    0:00 / 6:54
    Instaread

    Peter Baber takes a look at the Airstream World Traveler 22RB, a caravan which is aimed at the European market.

    Verdict

    The first time I saw an Airstream up close I couldn’t believe how far removed it was from what European customers are used to. This new model seems much closer to the mark. It still has quirks, but it’s beautifully built. It’s expensive, but if kudos matters to you and you have the budget (and a heavy enough tow car), why not go for it?

    Pros

    • Well built
    • Huge kudos value

    Cons

    • Expensive
    • Still some quirks

    For many people an Airstream is the ultimate in caravanning.

    The trouble is that in the past few years you’d need to part with a six-figure sum to get a new one of these luxury caravans.

    Earlier this year, however, a new model arrived at Lowdhams – currently Airstream’s only UK dealer. The Airstream World Traveler 22RB has been designed to be more affordable and appeal to an international audience. More models should be on the way later this year. I went to Lowdhams to take a look.

    Pitch and set-up

    The Airstream World Traveler 22RB looks pristine, but it achieves that look by not having any grab handles. Given that it weighs 1800kg unladen, you are going to need a caravan motor mover.

    The awning can be rolled out with supports attached at each end to the caravan. It looks more stylish and is possibly more secure than average. There’s also a hot and cold external shower.

    It also has its own onboard water tanks for both fresh and grey water. The onboard toilet isn’t a cassette toilet as such – it’s connected to a 41-litre black waste tank, emptied via a hose to a portable Fiamma waste-water tank that you empty the same way as you do with a cassette (see: how to empty a caravan toilet if you need a reminder).

    Lounge in the Airstream World Traveler 22RB

    You notice the sound deadening effect of the semi-monocoque design of this caravan as soon as you walk in. Headroom is impressive, too, which is always going to be important in the best caravans. The only seating area is immediately to the right.

    Lowdhams plans to enhance the backrest cushions pictured here with something that looks more traditionally European, curving around the corner. It also plans to replace the felt-effect sliding locker doors with acrylic ones, and put uplighters inside the lockers.

    That should create a pleasing effect at night, to add to the existing downlighters under the locker, and the four large LEDs that run down the centre of the ceiling, all of which can be dimmed.

    The clip-on table is sturdy. There are USB ports in the little cubbyhole next to the offside settee, and the mains socket, like all the mains sockets in this van, is designed to work in the UK, Europe, and America. To the left of the door you will find controls for a Bluetooth sound system. This van also has an inbuilt air conditioner.

    Kitchen in the Airstream World Traveler 22RB

    The side kitchen has an impressive amount of workspace – and you get an extension. It’s well lit, too.

    There’s a sturdy sink, complete with a swan-neck tap with different spray controls. You only get a two-burner hob, and the caravan fridge is half height. But underneath the settee next to the door there is a ‘cooling drawer’, which works as either a freezer or a fridge.

    Beds in the Airstream World Traveler 22RB

    For those who are looking for the best 4-berth caravan, the sleeping setup will always be important.

    In the Airstream World Traveler 22RB, the single beds at the back are huge, although they don’t come with double bed-creating panels. The window in the back means you only get a minimal headboard, although the curves in the corner mean you should still be comfortable reading in bed – or watching the TV on its bracket.

    You make up the bed at the front by dislodging the table leg and swinging the table top down between the settees.

    Washroom in the Airstream World Traveler 22RB

    The washroom door shuts with a clunk just as impressive as the main door. There’s a shaving mirror facing you above a small corner basin, and the area is well lit via a large window with a blind.

    The neighbouring shower cubicle has quite a step to get into and feels a bit poky, due in part to intrusion from the wheelarch (which could be used as a seat).

    Storage in the Airstream World Traveler 22RB

    When it comes to your options for packing a caravan, there’s a large wardrobe, with a drawer underneath it, and overhead lockers at the front and back. Kitchen storage is impressive.

    The base unit includes three large drawers inside them, and a cupboard that contains a bin. There is plenty of space for pots, pans and kitchenware.

    The washroom has a small cupboard under the basin and a shallow one behind the mirror for cosmetics.

    Alternatives to consider

    You could always consider the Coachman Lusso IV, a tourer which launched at the February NEC Show. The four-berth provides good storage, comfortable seating and a large kitchen.

    Or there’s the Swift Elegance Grande 845, a spacious and well-equipped caravan which has Alde underfloor heating and an excellent washroom.

    • Berths: 4

    • Payload: Up to 300kg
